text: The milk reform: who really pays the price?   Every time they talk about agricultural reform, the story repeats itself: the agricultural lobby warns of a collapse, claims that the problem is not theirs at all, and promises that imports will not lower prices for the consumer. Now it's happening in the dairy farm.  When you examine the matter without slogans but only facts, you see this: the dairy industry in Israel is one of the planned and centralized markets that exist: 🔹 The state determines how much milk will be produced 🔹 Who will be able to produce 🔹 And at what minimum price the dairies must buy? There is no competition, no entry of new players, and almost no imports - because of suffocating tariffs. And the result? High prices for the consumer, without direct connection to production efficiency.  Even the "target price", which sounds neutral, is structured so that it is strongly influenced by small and expensive dairy farms - some of which do not participate in the cost survey at all.  The proposed reform does not "eliminate agriculture", but changes the rules of the game: instead of closed quotas - protected liters at a lower price, opening the market, and creating an incentive for inefficient dairy farms to retire with compensation. And at the same time - a real possibility for importing and introducing new manufacturers.  And those who claim that imports "do not pass on to the consumer" - should look at the fish market after the removal of tariffs in 2016 and 2022, frozen fish prices fell by 8.3%, while other food products jumped by more than 22%.  The question now is: does the state manage a closed market for the benefit of an organized group, or does it open it to competition so that a basic product like milk is sold at a fair price?  The ball is in the court of the decision makers.  To the column by Ran Fitosi, economist and researcher of regulation in the Kohalat forum, in the first source >> https://www.makorrishon.co.il/news/economy/article/242896

text: The sword is back: on patience, roots and national resilience An interesting article by the researcher and translator Eli Kanin on the deep meanings of October 7 - not only as a military event, but a defining moment in Jewish history and global geopolitics. Kenin shows how the saber - that old Israeli symbol that seems to have been forgotten, came back to life in response to the war. Not through propaganda, but through spontaneous behavior: hundreds of thousands who were called to defend, fifty-year-old reservists who returned to their units, and a solidarity that surprised everyone, especially the enemy.  In his article, Kenin analyzes the war in three dimensions: historical: the connection between October 7 and the raid on Khyber in 628. Geopolitical: how the Palestinians lost militarily but won in the world narrative. Cultural: the conflict between the Israeli culture of life and the Islamist worldview.  Israel rediscovered the quality of patience - not as a weakness but as a strength. Our enemies have always thought that time is on their side and Israel must learn the same quality, while maintaining the clarity of the path. Recommended reading for those who want to understand in depth what really happened on October 7 and what its long-term significance is. text: Why do excellent teachers run away from the education system? The data revealed by Dr. Naama Avidan, an education researcher at the Ecclesiastical Forum, in the Knesset's Education Committee should turn on a red light for all of us. If you were wondering why there is a severe shortage of teachers, here are two of the main reasons: 1. Extreme seniority gaps: a beginning teacher in Israel earns only 45% of the salary of a seasoned teacher, for exactly the same work. This is the highest gap in all OECD countries (where the average is 61%). The message to the young teachers is clear: the only way to raise the salary is to simply age in the system 2. Bureaucratic barriers to personal contracts: instead of allowing flexibility in salary to attract quality personnel, the system piles up difficulties. A teacher who wants to switch to a personal contract and improve his conditions, is often required to leave the system, go through a "cooling off period" and only then return. The current structure of the education system doesn't reward excellence, but mediocrity. If we don't change the rules of the game, we will continue to lose our best forces. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zuhaIIfJhbc

text: The Knesset is currently discussing a reform that could change the face of transportation in Israel: the introduction of real, competitive and smart cooperative transportation. The move is aimed at freeing a stuck and protected market, lowering prices, encouraging innovation and giving consumers back the freedom of choice.   A taxi license is not a right granted forever, and just as the country has opened other markets to competition - it is right to do so here as well, with fair and graduated compensation for the drivers who will be harmed.  The world's experience is clear: in cities that adopted collaborative transportation, there was a decrease in congestion, less pollution, less searches for parking - and more free time for citizens. Smart integration with public transportation provides a solution for the last mile and improves mobility and employment.   Taxi drivers are experienced professionals, but in a free society the decision should be in the hands of the consumers - to choose between an old and professional service and a new and sometimes cheaper or more available alternative.   The time has come to release the regulatory bottleneck and allow Israelis to move efficiently, freely and at a fair price. text: The Chaos in the North and the State of Israel / Elitzur The chaos on our northern border requires us to look beyond the fence, to the historical and complex space of the Levant (Al-Sham), which includes Syria, Lebanon, Jordan and Israel. This is a multi-layered area of ​​identities, ethnicities and peoples, where history shows how fragile stability is.  The city of Damascus was called in Arabic "A-Sham", a term which according to Maimonides translates to "Land of Israel", a testimony to the depth of the historical and cultural connections in the area.  Since the Ottoman occupation in the 16th century, through the reign of Ibrahim Pasha in the 19th century, and until the division of the region by Mark Sykes and Charles Francois Georges Picot between Great Britain and France, the borders of the Middle East were often drawn without matching the ethnic and religious reality on the ground.  Understanding the historical background and the complexity of the space is essential to correctly interpret the events around us today, and formulate a sober policy for the future.  🔗Read the full article from the collection Two years after the October 7 massacre - disillusionment, change and struggle.  https://www.kohelet.org.il/article/%d7%94%d7%9b%d7%90%d7%95%d7%a1-%d7%91%d7%a6%d7% a4%d7%95%d7%9f-%d7%95%d7%9e%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%aa-%d7%99%d7%a9%d7%a8%d7%90%d7%9c/

But after the thanks, she also asked for forgiveness: "Forgive my father, and the 46 whose lives were kidnapped and murdered by Hamas during the war. Sorry you left the house on your feet. Sorry, even after the omission, and after the horror of the Shiv'a in October, you could have been saved, and they didn't do it." Noam repeated and said: The people returned the kidnapped, and the people will also bring about the correction.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Yesterday Uri Danino was supposed to celebrate his 27th birthday, but he will forever remain 25. Uri was born on January 31, 1999 in Jerusalem, the son of Einav and Elhanan. He was the brother of Isaac, David, Aaron and Hodia. Uri was an especially loved person, with a big heart and lots of friends, someone who was always there for others, at any hour.  Uri loved nature and field trips, spending time with friends and living the moment. Black coffee was almost a hobby for him, and those who knew him spoke of a man who radiates joy in life, kindness and mutual guarantee. He planned to start studying electrical engineering, and he had dreams and plans for the future.  On October 7, 2023 Uri was at the Nova party. He was already on his way to safety, but chose to turn back, into the fire, to save lives. Uri rescued Mia and Iti Regev and Omar Shem Tov in his car, but on their way they were ambushed by terrorists, and they were all kidnapped to Gaza.  Uri was held captive by Hamas for about 11 months. Even in the most impossible conditions, he continued to show responsibility, courage and concern for others, and fought so that his wounded friends would receive treatment.  On August 29, 2024, the late Uri Danino was brutally murdered by Hamas terrorists, in a tunnel in the Rafah area, along with Carmel Gat, Hersh Goldberg-Poulin, Aden Yerushalmi, Alex Lobnov and the late Almog Sarosi.  Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Uri, a young man who, in the moment of truth, chose not to save only himself, but to go back to save others. This choice defines who he was, and the values ​​he left behind.  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Today Itai Chen should have celebrated his 22nd birthday, but he will forever remain 19 years old. Itai was born on February 2, 2004, the second son of Ruby and Hagit Chen and a younger brother to Roy. Later he got to be a big brother to Alon.  Itay grew up in Netanya and was a promising athlete. He liked to play basketball, climb climbing walls and travel around the country. When he got to high school he studied in the excellence class.   As a teenager, Itai was involved in social activities and was a youth leader. Although he was injured during his duty as an instructor, he insisted on continuing in the role. During the long vacation, Itay worked as an instructor at a summer camp at Tel Aviv University, where he met Netta Simon, who became his partner.   In August 2022, Itai enlisted as an armored fighter in the 77th Battalion of the glorious 7th Brigade.   On the morning of October 7th, I went out with the members of the tank team with him to fight the many terrorists who infiltrated the Nahal Oz sector. The team fought for hours, shot, ran over and stopped waves of terrorists, while constantly moving between different points, thus saving many lives. The traces of the tank's journey left on the ground were silent testimony to the team's initiative and determined fighting. Thanks to their fierce fighting, together with other heroes, they managed to prevent more crowds of terrorists from reaching Nahal Oz, Kibbutz Sa'ad, Kfar Gaza, and the main road.  Sergeant Itai Chen fell during the heroic battle and was kidnapped. Along with him were also kidnapped the tank commander, Capt. Daniel Peretz, the 14th, and the survivor of the captivity, Maj. Gen. Matan Engrest. The late Sergeant Tomer Leibovitz, a member of the fourth team, also fell in the heroic battle that morning.  Today, we will stop for a moment and we will all remember Itai, the Lion King, who loved the State of Israel and fell in battle to protect its citizens. The heroic warrior with a heart of gold, who gave of himself to all.  In his memory 💔 @EmailRubychen @hagitchen Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today, with the ascension of the family of the late Rani Goili to the grave at the end of the seven days, one of the most terrible and painful periods the people of Israel have known ends. The family, friends, comrades-in-arms and Israeli police officers and many others gathered this morning at the fresh grave of Rani Goili, a hero of Israel and defender of the unknown.   Rani, the last remaining abductee in Gaza, was finally laid to rest - not as we had hoped, but as it had to happen: at home, on his land, surrounded by the love of his family and people.  This is a moment of deep mourning, but also of closing a painful national circle. 255 abductees were returned to Israel. 87 were placed as victims, each one a world and full, each of them an open wound in the hearts of the families and in the heart of the entire country.  The headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees ends its activity with a sense of unrelenting pain for all those who could be with us here today and are not, but also with a clear knowledge: the struggle was waged in the name of the values ​​of the State of Israel and the people of Israel. The values ​​of mutual guarantee, social solidarity and the duty to return home every abductee regardless of religion, race and gender, soldiers and civilians, living or dead.   This historic struggle for their return will be engraved in the national memory as a reminder of the unimaginable human cost of October 7, and of the deep commitment of Israeli society to the families, the missing and the missing. It was also the beautiful hour of the people of Israel who took to the streets en masse, all over the country in the name of these values.  On this day, we will also cherish the soldiers and women of the IDF and all the security forces for a very long and bloody fight. We will send a blessing of recovery to all those wounded in body and soul and we will forever be grateful to all the bereaved families who lost the most precious to them of all. We bow our heads to the Goyili family and to all the families of the martyrs, and pray that we will never have to fight like this again. This is the time for restoration, for all the people of Israel. Photography: Uriel Ibn Sapir Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Family members, friends, fellow soldiers, Israel Police officers, and many others gathered this morning at the fresh grave of Master Sgt. Ran Gvili, as his family visited his final resting place following the conclusion of the “Shivaa” (the Jewish seven-day mourning period).  This is a moment of profound grief, but also a painful national reckoning. All 255 hostages held in Gaza, including all 251 hostages abducted on October 7 were returned to Israel. 87 were returned deceased - each a world unto themselves, each an open wound in the hearts of their families and of the nation as a whole.  The Hostages and Missing Families Forum is concluding its activities with deep grief for all those who should have been with us today and are not, and with the conviction that the struggle was carried out in the name of Israel’s core values: mutual responsibility, solidarity, and the obligation to bring every hostage home - soldier or civilian, living or deceased.  This historic effort will remain etched in the national memory as a reminder of the price paid on October 7 and of the profound commitment shown by Israeli society.  On this day, we also honor the soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces and all security forces for a long and bloody campaign, extend wishes for healing to all those wounded in body and spirit, and express enduring gratitude to the bereaved families who paid the heaviest price of all.  We bow our heads to the Gvili family and to all families of the fallen, and pray that the people of Israel will never again be forced to endure such a struggle. This is a moment for mourning and for healing for the entire nation.  Photo credit: Uriel Even Sapir  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Forever young - today Shani Lok should have celebrated her 25th birthday, but she will forever remain 22. Shani was born on February 7, 2001 in Moshav Adrat. Daughter of Nissim and Ricarda (Ricky) who came from Germany and fell in love with Israel and Judaism. Sister to Adi to Amit and Or. At the age of two, she moved to live with her family in the settlement of Serigi.  Shani was a beautiful, creative and independent girl, with a big and compassionate heart. From a young age, her love for art sprouted. Whether music, dance, writing, fashion design, hair design or sewing. In high school she combined theoretical studies alongside art studies. When she matured, she moved to Tel Aviv, where she lived with friends, studied graphic design and worked as a tattoo artist.  Shani's other love was to travel and get to know other languages ​​and cultures. During her travels she participated in many music festivals around the world and in one of them she met Orion Hernandez Rado, a talented music producer from Mexico, who became her partner and even came with her to the Nova festival.   On the morning of October 7, Shani and Orion tried to escape the terror of the missiles. They were traveling in a car with their friend Keshet Kasruti, but unfortunately the terrorists closed in on them. The three friends were murdered and Orion and Shani were kidnapped to Gaza.   Her big dream of setting up a big studio, where she will do tattoos and dreadlocks, and sell clothes designed by her, especially clothes for festivals, she will no longer be able to fulfill.   Riki's mother said: "For dinner on Friday. On October 6, before the terrible day, I told her to come with Orion. We didn't meet him and we really wanted to get to know him. She said that they were going to a party with bad guys and that they wouldn't be enough, but she promised that she would come with him to dinner the following Friday. Who knew, there wouldn't be a next Friday."  Today, let's stop for a moment and we will all remember the beautiful and lively Shani, who loved music and danced through life, until the terrible day when the melody of her life was cruelly stopped.   In memory of 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The Hostages and Missing Families Forum was established on October 8, 2023, less than 24 hours after the devastating attack of October 7th. The Forum, a nonprofit organization founded by hostage families, set itself the goal of bringing home all hostages, regardless of religion, race, or gender. On day 843 of the war, the Forum completed its mission with the return of the last hostage.  Thousands of volunteers joined the Forum, including senior figures from the security, legal, media, health, and diplomatic sectors. Working closely with government ministries, the IDF, foreign governments, and hundreds of communities worldwide, they mobilized rapidly under extreme wartime conditions to achieve unprecedented results. The Forum operates around the clock with two core divisions. The advocacy division leads strategic communications, diplomacy, grassroots organizing, business engagement, and creative campaigns at both Israeli and international levels. The family services division provides logistical, medical, and emotional support while coordinating legal counsel, medical documentation, and family advocacy activities.  💛Farewell💛  The Hostages Forum was established to bring the hostages home and closed upon full completion of its mission with the return of the last hostage. The Forum succeeded in the sacred, values-driven, and moral mission it set for itself: returning 255 of our brothers and sisters from Hamas captivity, some to rehabilitation, some for burial, thanks to the support and involvement of the people of Israel, world Jewry, countless individuals around the world, and assistance from the business sector. Special thanks to the tens of thousands of volunteers and activists in Israel and worldwide.  The effort to keep the hostage issue in public consciousness could not have succeeded without the mobilization of media outlets and journalists who understood the magnitude of the moment and the mission, working day after day, each in their own way, to amplify the voices of those silenced in Hamas tunnels. Even on the most difficult days, they persevered and carried the burden of the mission shoulder to shoulder with us. We thank them for their fruitful, values-driven, and successful cooperation, even when fraught with challenges.  We will forever mourn the destruction and loss inflicted upon us by our enemies and eternally grieve the loss of 46 hostages who could have returned to us alive. We mourn all 87 deceased hostages together with hundreds of our fallen civilians and soldiers, and we extend eternal gratitude to their families for their sacrifice. We send wishes for complete healing to soldiers wounded in body and soul and embrace them with all our hearts.  Day 843, the day the last hostage returned, was the first day since 2014 on which there were no hostages in Gaza. May there never be again, not in Gaza, not anywhere. But if, God forbid, there ever are, let every parent know: we stand together, and mutual responsibility and solidarity are our guiding principles. The people of Israel have proven they will never abandon one another held in captivity.   Thank you 🙏   "Thus says the Lord: Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work shall be rewarded, says the Lord, and they shall come back from the land of the enemy." (Jeremiah 31:15)  Photo credit: Nadav Cohen Yonatan, Paulina Patimer, Adar Eyal, Eyal Radoshitzky  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and missing persons - the abductees' square The headquarters began its activity in the museum tower, and later moved to the Check Point building, which hosted the headquarters until its closure. The Museum Square, courtesy of the Tel Aviv Municipality, was converted into the Kidnapped Square and became, next to the Ariela House, the central space of the headquarters and the families.  The square was a second home for the members of the families, a focal point for rallies, press conferences, exhibitions and events, and a place of pilgrimage for supporters of the struggle from Israel and the world.  The square was also the beating heart of the struggle and the direct connection with the public, who came to it for thousands of events - rallies, Shabbat receptions, birthdays, prayers and statements to the media and was a space of support, reinforcement and mutual guarantee. This is also the place where the Israeli and international media operated, alongside ongoing activities and trainings for volunteer teams.  In the nearby Ariela house, the "Family Room" was established - a quiet, protected and intimate space, where dozens of volunteers provided hot food, activities for children and a meeting place for the families, allowing them to be together, strengthen and feel at home. text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the health system and the resilience team The health system worked continuously and intensively from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee, while providing comprehensive health care for the families of the abductees, the returnees and all the activities of the headquarters.  The organization developed a multidisciplinary professional doctrine in the field of "health of abductees and families of abductees", published reports and articles and made accessible the health, medical and mental implications of abduction to decision makers in Israel and around the world, with an emphasis on humanitarian and international organizations.  At the same time, a unique professional and public language was formulated to understand the multidimensional damage of the kidnapping and to sharpen the sense of urgency to return all the abductees, alive and dead.   The organization regularly accompanied the families, initiated collaborations with the health system and treatment providers, motivated the health and scientific community in Israel and the world, and took part in professional initiatives, conferences and public activities. In addition to this, he identified and mapped the unique needs of the families of the abductees and the survivors of the captivity, worked for professional advocacy and the exploitation of rights, and accompanied rehabilitation and long-term support, while laying the foundation for future research on the effects of the abduction on the health of the families and the returnees.  The resilience team was established immediately with the establishment of the headquarters, when about ten women and therapists were stationed to help. First the resilience team members joined all the intense protest activities, marches, rallies, demonstrations, and provided emotional support as needed. The caregivers were in close contact with most of the families and their door was open to help anyone who needed it at any hour of the day.  As the struggle dragged on and the headquarters was organized, mental support gradually became structured: a clinic was opened for urgent and short interventions and diagnosis. The clinic has created a significant therapeutic sequence with external therapists for long-term treatments.  In addition, the headquarters teams who worked closely with the families with a huge emotional investment, and especially the family teams, the media teams, the family room team and the field headquarters, received a therapist who joined the teams for counseling, training, and individual help.   As the struggle continued and its consequences on the mental state of the family members, diverse activities were added: group therapy for homogeneous groups, such as families of martyrs, mothers of abductees, young people, etc.; days of respite; Retreats for homogenous groups with two-three days of therapeutic activity and consolidation and relaxation activities. In all of these meetings, of all types, ties were tightened and familiarity and trust with the families expanded, and the staff of caregivers remained available even for informal interventions during the protest activities. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - the legal department The legal department has been active since the establishment of the headquarters on a variety of levels, in Israel and in the international arena, to promote the fight for the return of the abductees and to protect their rights and the rights of their families.  The department led the promotion of legislation and policies concerning the rights of abductees, returnees and their families; Worked to raise the issue of the abductees and Hamas crimes in international institutions, led by the UN; and protection of the rights of the abductees and their families as victims of a crime against the state authorities.  As part of its activities in the international arena, the department submitted an official complaint to the International Criminal Court against the leaders of Hamas, demanding justice for war crimes, sexual abuse and abuse of kidnapped children and the children of the kidnapped families, for which international legal recognition was registered. In addition, the legal team initiated senior visits from the UN and the Red Cross to Israel, meetings with the families of the abductees, assisted in the legal battle against UNRWA, and resulted in the conviction of the spreaders of false rumors in the Israeli courts.   Alongside this, the department worked to maintain privacy and medical confidentiality, assisted in the mapping and extraction of rights and ongoing legal support for families, and took care of all the legal aspects required for the operations of the headquarters. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the abducted and the missing - strategy The level of struggle and the strategic consultation formed the core of the activities of the headquarters of the families of the abductees. Leading women and professionals in their fields, of a variety of ages and professional experience, veteran Israelis and new immigrants served on the floor.  The chief strategist together with the strategic consulting team formulated the policy of the headquarters, managed and carried out dozens of studies to form public perceptions in Israel and abroad, examined the extent to which the headquarters met the goals and objectives set for it by the families of the abductees and adapted the strategy to target audiences, sectors and policy makers around the world.   The strategic team included experts in the fields of media, international, religious, ultra-Orthodox, Knesset and government, Arab countries and international law.  The headquarters of the families of the abductees was run through its democratically authorized institutions. Strategic decisions were made by majority vote by the plenum of representatives of the families of the abductees, while the implementation of the policy decided upon was entrusted to the faithful hands of the assembly - a limited selection of representatives from among the families.  The headquarters operated one of the largest, most sophisticated and versatile content, media, data and advertising systems that have operated in Israel since time immemorial.   At the beginning of its journey, the headquarters was assisted by external offices, but as of April 2024, an independent advertising, creative, media purchasing, production, post-production and ideation system was built at the headquarters. Senior women and men of the advertising world worked alongside talented and young talents to manage an unprecedented advertising campaign in Israel and abroad.  In the field of information, Israeli communication teams, international communication and the social department worked at the headquarters. Elite units of information that handled the aggregate of tens of thousands of inquiries from the media in Israel and around the world. The departments initiated media exposure in accordance with the strategy of the headquarters and in accordance with the events that accompanied us from the October 7th until the return of the last abductee. The social network established collaborations with the most powerful media organizations and leading platforms. The department was a cutting edge of creativity and groundbreaking thinking in all fields.  Photographs: The Seventh Day of Iron Swords (credit Rani Graff) 02.01.2025 Painting buildings yellow. text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and the missing - spokespeople and Israeli media The Israeli communications department was a central axis in the struggle for the return of the abductees and has operated continuously since the establishment of the headquarters. The department led the full media response: formulating and distributing messages to the media, mobilizing public opinion in Israel and around the world, conducting thousands of interviews and articles on all media platforms, preparing and accompanying the families of the abductees to public and media appearances.  The media team led coverage of hundreds of rallies, marches, statements and events for the abductees, day and night, on Saturdays and holidays. The team led special broadcast days, dozens of coverage points at the same time and led coverage like no other in Israel. The subject of the abductees was present in tens of thousands of items and articles on television, radio, written and online press, in podcasts, playlists and in every possible way.  The team led to unprecedented achievements in the scope of media exposure in all its aspects and thanks to them, among other things, the subject of the abductees did not drop from the public agenda from the beginning of the war until the return of the last abductee.  The team provided a professional and available response to the media around the clock, and worked to create a consistent and clear public presence of the abductees issue, while adapting the messages to the moment, the scene and the changing needs of the struggle.  Through the in-depth work of dozens of workers and volunteers, the media served as a significant tool for the presence of the abductees, for connecting the public to the struggle and for leading a responsible, humane and valuable discourse throughout. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Rani Goili should have celebrated his 27th birthday, but he will forever remain 24 years old. Rani was born on February 11, 1999. Ben Latlik and Itzik Goili, a younger brother to Omari. Shira later joined and Rennie was awarded the title of "big brother". Ketam and Luna, Rani's favorite boxers, have always been part of the family.  From his childhood, Rani was a rare combination of tenderness and strength, sensitivity and responsibility, joy of life and a sense of mission. A young and dignified man who always spoke at the level of the poor with a powerful and calm presence. Rani liked to play the guitar, ride motorcycles and exercise. He was always surrounded by a large circle of friends, true friends who stood by each other, one for the other.  From his youth, Rani knew that he wanted to serve in a significant role and when he enlisted in the IDF, he volunteered to serve in the Golani Brigade, where he stood out as a brave, dedicated and purposeful fighter. After his release from the IDF, he chose to continue serving, and enlisted in the Israel Police. He served as a fighter in the Negev YSM unit in the southern district and passed the tests for the army, however, due to his young age, he had to wait until he was 25. During his service, he stood out for his courage, coolness and extraordinary dedication to the safety of the citizens.  On the morning of October 7th, Rani was injured at home with a fractured shoulder following a motorcycle accident, but as soon as he heard about the infiltration of the terrorists, he put on a uniform and went out to help his friends from the unit in fighting. During that morning, Rani led dozens of survivors of the Nova festival to safety, and later joined the fighters and the standby squad of Kibbutz Alumim who tried to stop the dozens of terrorists who tried to infiltrate the kibbutz. Rani fought with strength and ferocity at the front of the battle at the entrance to the kibbutz and after a stubborn battle, and only after he ran out of ammunition, Rani fell in battle and was kidnapped to Gaza.  Today, let's pause for a moment and all of us remember Major Ran Goyili, a hero of Israel and a 'defender of the unknown', the one with the big smile and the broad shoulders. The sociable guy, funny and loved by his friends. A huge heart, a true friend, one who always saw those who were left behind, and was the first to lend a hand. In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the kidnapped and missing - diplomacy and international missions The international department led one of the largest and most significant international moves in the history of the State of Israel. The department included hundreds of employees and volunteers, among them diplomats, former ambassadors, former MKs, academics and media, and field staffs in 50 countries. As part of the international diplomatic and legal work, hundreds of delegations of families of abductees and survivors of captivity went out, mainly to the USA and key European countries, with the aim of making their voices heard and influencing policy. Members of the families met with presidents, prime ministers, foreign ministers, elected officials and officials Key in the international arena, and reached the decision-making centers in Washington, New York, London, Berlin, Paris, Brussels, Geneva and The Hague. Each delegation was accompanied by extensive communication, careful logistical planning and close coordination in Israel and abroad. the lives and the spaces, and changed the public discourse in the country. The peak of the effort was recorded in the meetings held by President Trump with the survivors of the captivity and the family members and in the speeches given by the special envoy Witkoff, Trump's son-in-law Kushner and his daughter Ivanka in the Kidnapped Square in front of half a million participants.  Along with the many trips, many meetings of the families of the abductees and the returnees with diplomats and government officials from dozens of countries around the world were held at the headquarters and in the square. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the headquarters of the families for the return of the kidnapped and the missing - social department The social team has been active since the establishment of the headquarters and led the assimilation of the call Bring Them Home Now, which became the name of the pages and the hashtag associated with the struggle of the families of the abductees.   The team established and operated pages in Hebrew and English on all social networks: Facebook, Instagram, X, Tiktok, LinkedIn and YouTube, and spread the voice of the families of the abductees through original content, interviews, live broadcasts, parades and rallies in Israel and around the world. The headquarters pages on the international platforms reached almost a million followers and in Israeli about half a million, with tens of millions of views per month. Videos uploaded by the headquarters received millions of views in Israel and around the world, and at the peak - over 200 million monthly views on Instagram alone.  The international activity reached followers from Europe to the USA, Australia and the Far East. A uniform and identifiable visual language was developed, which made it possible to identify the headquarters' contents on any platform and in any language.  The team led activities in front of influencers in Israel and around the world. Together, millions of people were exposed to the contents of the headquarters, shared the stories of the abductees and assisted in a joint and strong call for their return.  During the 843 days of the struggle for the return of the abductees, over 50 volunteers took part in the team's activities, which led to unprecedented achievements and the presence of the abductees everywhere and at all times. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the family headquarters for the return of the abducted and the missing - field headquarters in Israel and around the world hundreds of field headquarters were established in Israel and around the world. Good people who initiated, led and promoted activities for the return of the abductees all over the country and in many other countries as well. Each headquarters has a character and color adapted to the community and the families of the abductees from the area.   The activists led diverse activities: from daily identification shifts at intersections, weekly rallies, fundraising stands and making the issue of the abductees and the struggle accessible to the local community. Initiate collaborations with the local government, the education system, youth movements, local businesses and paint the country yellow. The thousands of volunteers all over the country and the world made sure that at every event and conference the subject of the abductees was mentioned and the fight for their return continued.  Many initiatives were started in the field headquarters such as the yellow shirt in schools on September 1, operation of national convoys and flagging and signage throughout the country.  The operatives and activities of the field headquarters operated on a full volunteer basis, day and night and on Saturdays and holidays, until the return of the last abductee. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: On November 2, 2023, a call went out from the headquarters of the families of the abductees inviting everyone to take part in the empty chair display - until everyone returns home, a yellow chair is placed at the entrance to public areas. Businesses, public and private companies, government bodies and organizations, municipalities, councils and local authorities, educational institutions and cooperative employment buildings - placed a yellow chair at the entrance to their offices. In the main squares of the cities and at the entrance gates of many settlements, displays of chairs with the pictures of the abductees were set up, and the yellow chair also reached the Shabbat and holiday tables in many homes.  The "Ketar" company, which until October 7, 2023 did not market yellow plastic chairs, created during the war 25,000 chairs that were placed across the length and breadth of the country as a symbol of the abductees.   Last weekend, after all 255 abductees from Gaza were resettled, the central display of the yellow chairs was also removed from the abductees' square, but in our hearts all 87 abductees will always remain empty. Those whose chairs remain forever orphaned.  We returned. Now get up.  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: One year ago today, Sasha Trupanov, Yair Horn and Shagyi Dekel Chen returned home. With tears we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones. Now that there are no more abductees in Gaza, our mission continues: we must help them get up.   We must help all families get up.   We must help the country to rise.      We returned. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Exactly one year ago Sasha Troufanov, Iair Horn, and Sagui Dekel-Chen crossed the border and returned home. Through tears, we watched them fall into the arms of their loved ones.   Since then, we’ve watched them begin to piece their lives back together, bravely sharing some of the ordeals they endured in the hell of Gaza.   Almost immediately, they joined the fight to bring the rest home, until the last hostage.   Their strength and courage helped unite the Israeli people and supporters around the world.   Now that there are no hostages left in Gaza, our work continues.  We must help them heal.  We must help all the families heal.  We must help our people heal.   Now, we rise. 💛  Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

text: Today Itai Sbirsky should have celebrated his 41st birthday, but he will forever remain 38. Itai was born in Bari on February 17, 1985, third child to Rafi and Orit, brother to Merev and Yonatan, and later also to Yuval.  With me was a curious and sensitive boy, with golden curls and a shy half smile.  Already in his childhood photos, you can see his kind eyes and the inquisitive look, sensitive to the environment. A gifted athlete, starting with Barry's basketball team, through tennis lessons and ending with soccer. His classmates in the "Apple" class say that he was one level above everyone else. Itay was also a die-hard fan of Maccabi Tel Aviv. In his youth, his love for music developed. He studied voice development and enjoyed playing the guitar and piano.  Itay served in the air traffic control unit (IA). After his release and the trip to India, he moved to Tel Aviv and began studying at the university. Along with his studies, he continued personal development processes and fell in love with Brazilian jiu-jitsu, which became an integral part of his life. From a young age, Itay dealt with philosophical questions, with curiosity and a willingness to listen to the other side and learn new things. This is how he came to the Satya method; first as a trainee and later as a trainer himself. Friends and family They say that the method allowed him to express his wonderful ability to listen deeply to what he heard. He was the perfect uncle to his parents and a grandson who made sure to visit his grandmother as much as possible. On Friday, October 6th, the brutal attack on the kibbutz caught him At his mother Orit's. They both locked themselves in the MMD, with gunshots and shouts in Arabic all around them. The family members kept in touch through the joint WhatsApp group. Slowly and gradually the ties were severed: first with Rafi, then with Itai, and last was Orit. She sent a heart, and another heart.  Orit and Rafi were murdered in Bari on October 7. Itay was kidnapped alive. On the 97th day of his captivity, the building where he was held, along with Noa Argamani and the late Yossi Sharabi, collapsed on them. Itay survived and managed to rescue himself. Days later, after 99 days in captivity in Gaza, he was murdered by his captors. With the release of Noa Argamani, who was with Itay in captivity until his last moments, we learned that even in the inhumane conditions in which they were held, Itay remained who he was: he showed resourcefulness and recruited the All his powers and abilities to survive under constant threat, and he had the courage to be there for others as well. Today, let's stop for a moment and remember him, a man of connection and humanity. Open, curious, and always looking to see others. In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: The story of the families headquarters for the return of the abducted and missing - the family team The family team was the beating heart of the families, a source of warmth, comfort and unconditional love. The team connected the families with the professionals, maintained direct and daily contact with them and constituted a central address for the families for any need.  The team leaders accompanied, coordinated and supported the families while responding to their needs, coordinated between parties at the headquarters and outside, assisted in the preparation for formal and informal meetings, delegations abroad for leaders and government officials in Israel and around the world.  The families know how to tell about the endless support and generosity of the team members. They were a reason and an incentive to get up in the morning even on dark days. With their help, the helplessness of many families turned into a sense of ability, despair into hope and sorrow and loneliness into companionship and comfort.   Thanks to the team's work, and its ability to connect family members from all sectors with women and professionals of all types and fields, it was possible for families to maintain both their dignity and their unique voice, and to place it at the center of the public struggle for the return of their loved ones in Israel and around the world. author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Hadar Goldin should have celebrated his 35th birthday, but forever he will remain 23 years old. Hadar, son of Simcha and Lea Goldin, was born on February 18, 1991. Five minutes after he went live, his twin brother Tzur joined him. At the family home, their older brothers were already waiting for them - Ayelet and my father-in-law (Menachem).   Hadar and Tzur brought a lot of light wherever they went. Together they learned to play music, paint and sculpt, together they went to Bnei Akiva and turned from apprentices to instructors and together they went to the "Bnei David" preparatory school with my husband.   When they enlisted in the IDF, their paths diverged, Tsur for the paratroopers and Hadar for the Givat patrol. Hadar was a team leader at the end of the training, a reconnaissance and intelligence course, an officer preparation course, and an officer course in basic training. After the officers' course, he wanted to be a commander in training the patrol's rookies and turn them into fighters. Hadar instilled in his soldiers and subordinates the values he grew up with - friendship Courage among the team members, love and help to others will lead the team to an outstanding team. And then he reached the realization of his ambition - during his military service, Hadar proposed to his girlfriend Edna Sarosi, while he was waiting with his soldiers in the assembly area, and at the same time he arranged the invitation. At 08:00 a.m., a ceasefire was declared shortly after Hamas launched two mortar bombs at 09:05 a.m., and three of the force's soldiers were killed in the battle: Maj. Lial Gideoni. Hadar was kidnapped through a tunnel and held in Gaza for 4,118 days.  Today, we will stop for a moment and we will all remember Lt. Hadar Goldin, who in his smile, in his paintings, in his writings, and in the hearts of his family, apprentices and soldiers, left his will bearing the banner of loving people and doing good. As Hadar himself used to say: "You have two options; either mess with yourself, or do something better."  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: Today Alex Lubanov should have celebrated his 35th birthday, but forever he will remain 33 years old. Alexander (Alex) Lubanov, was born on 18.02.1991 in Russia. When he was 8 years old, he immigrated to Israel with his family. Alex fit in wonderfully at school, was a sociable, self-confident and ambitious child. He always set goals for himself and enjoyed achieving them. His love for the kitchen led him to work after his military service as a cook at the Fishenzon restaurant in the marina in Ashkelon, where in 2013 he met Michal who worked there as a waitress. Over the years they fell in love and got married. His big dream was to open a restaurant on the beach.  Alex loved to travel very much. He joined the community "Subaru and Jeeps travel for free", and over the years he was among the leaders of the community. With the birth of his eldest son, Tom, in 2021, Alex combined his love for traveling with his love for his son. He would pick him up from kindergarten and they would go on jeep trips together. Alex regularly volunteered at the "Yadidis" organization, which provides first aid on the roads. He greatly assisted the army and the police in rescuing civilians and vehicles His friends and family always knew that he could be trusted in everything. In his spare time, Alex used to spend time with his family and friends. He loved diving, listening to music and cooking. On October 6, 2023, he was in charge of the bar and the bartenders On the morning of October 7, Alex reassured her that they were getting ready to go home. He decided to run away with his friends towards the forest near Kibbutz Bari. At around nine in the morning, his family received the news that Alex had been captured for 11 months Michal had their second son and named him Kai. Michal believed with all her heart that Alex would return home and get to know Kai. After the birth, she also asked to send a message to Alex: "I want to tell you that you have to come back and see how much Kai looks like you, how much Tom is waiting for you. You need to be strong, just as we are strong for you." On August 29, 2024, the terrorists guarding Alex Lubnov, Hersh Goldberg-Polin, Carmel Gat, Uri Danino, Aden Yerushalmi and Almog Sarosi murdered the six abductees in a tunnel in Gaza. Two days later, during an IDF operation in the Tel Sultan neighborhood of Rafah, their bodies were located and returned to Israel.  Alex left behind his wife Michal, his children Tom and Kai, his parents Oksana and Gregory and his brother Anton.   Today, we will stop for a moment and remember Alex. A guy with a big heart, a captivating smile, and a rollicking laugh full of joy. A moral and optimistic guy who loved nature, lived the sea and above all loved to help and contribute to others wholeheartedly.  In his memory 💔 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: With the recovery of all the hijackers we end the current activity of our page. After almost 28 months of non-stop struggle, day and night, we stop, take a breath and ask to say thank you. Thank you from the deepest place in my heart.  To each and every one of you who stood by the families. who refused to get used to it. who refused to give up. who refused to normalize.  who chose again and again not to look away.  You were with us in moments when the pain was greater than words. You echoed the cries. You bore the names. You gave way to tears, and also to the rare moments of light, when a small crack of hope finally appeared.  Anyone who took part in the struggle to return the abductees, is not just a supporter. He is part of history. Part of the most moral and valuable civil struggle that the State of Israel has known since its establishment.  You embraced the families as if they were your own. You carried them when they no longer had the strength left to carry themselves. And when it seemed like the world was moving on, you stayed.  Your likes. Your comments. Your shares. The words you wrote at two in the morning.  These were never small gestures.  They were a lifeline. They were a breath in the dark. They were evidence that even in the heart of the nightmare, humanity does not disappear. she struggles she is standing She illuminates.  One day they will ask: "Where were you during this time?"  And you can say, I was there. I was not silent. I didn't turn my back. I was part of the force that brought them home.  Thank you for carrying us when we ran out of air. Thank you for not giving up. Thank you for choosing Or.  You will always be a part of our hearts. And we will forever be grateful to you 💛 Bring Them Home Now by @BringThemHomeNow A @grttme project - Other backups: @Hallotme

author: BringThemHomeNow
text: After nearly 28 months of tireless efforts, and as this page now ceases its 24/7 activity, we want to say thank you, from the deepest place in our heart.  To every person who stood by the families, who refused to look away, who stayed. Everyone who took part in this fight to bring the hostages home became part of history, the largest civil movement in Israel since 1948.  You echoed the families’ pain, their cries, and even their rare moments of joy. You embraced the hostages and their families as if we were your family, too. You carried them when they could not carry themselves.  Your likes. Your comments. Your follows. Your shares.  They were never small gestures. Know this: they were a lifeline. They were a wave of human compassion that pierced through the darkest nightmare.  They were threads in a monumental force that moved mountains, touched every corner of the earth, and brought our loved ones home.  One day, when people ask, ‘Where were you during this time?’ You’ll be able to say: I was there. I did not stay silent. I was part of Bring Them Home Now. I helped bring them home.
